To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

all subjects who developed a smallpox-vesicle after vaccination also had detectable neutralizing-antiviral antibodies, and that subjects who were vaccinated with diluted vaccine developed significantly higher neutralizing antibody titers than did those who were vaccinated with undiluted vaccine.

all subjects who developed a lesion after vaccination developed neutralizing antibodies to smallpox virus by day 28, that subjects given a 1 :10 dilution of vaccine had higher titers of neutralizing antibodies than did subjects who were given a 1:5 dilution, and that subjects given either a 5- or 10-fold dilution of vaccine developed higher titers of antibody than did subjects who received undiluted vaccine.

all vaccinees who developed a vesicular lesion after vaccination also developed a plaque-reduction neutralization titer (PRNT) by day 28, and that subjects given a 1 :5 dilution had significantly higher PRNTs than those given an undiluted dose of smallpox-vaccinia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a vaccine for human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) type 1 infection.
the development and evaluation of a vaccine to protect against the potential threat posed by the use of variola virus in a bioterrorist act.
the development of a novel vaccine for HIV-1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 1 :10 dilution of the current smallpox vaccine stock (Dryvax) is the optimal vaccine dose to be used in the US civilian stockpile.

a 1 :10 dilution of the current smallpox-vaccination stock (Dryvax) is associated with a more robust humoral immune response to vaccination, as compared with undiluted vaccine, and that the 1 : 2 dilution of Dryvax currently recommended by the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices is associated with an intermediate response.
a 1 :5 dilution of small-pox vaccine results in higher antibody titers and a more robust immune response than does an undiluted dose of the same vaccine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neutralizing antibody titers were higher in subjects who received the 1:5 and 1:10 dilutions than in subjects who received undiluted vaccine and that neutralizing antibody titration may be a useful measure for the assessment of the quality of smallpox-vaccination lots.

the dose-response relationship for neutralizing-antigen titers was significant and that the relationship between neutralizing-antigens titers and the severity of adverse effects after vaccination also was significant.
a 1 :10 dilution of Dryvax vaccine produced a more robust immune response than did the undiluted vaccine and that a dose-response effect was observed with increasing vaccine doses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a dilution of 1 : 20 of the currently available smallpox vaccine would be expected to result in a neutralizing-antitoxin titer similar to that of undiluted smallpox vaccine.
the 1 : 3 dilution of Dryvax is a reasonable choice for vaccination of adults.
diluting Dryvax by 5 or 10 times does not compromise immune responses.
